StakeWise proxy changes and Curve asset routes
2 October 2026. All blockchain work is read-only. This study separates the StakeWise deposit pool, the
sETH2 token proxy and the Curve trading pools. The controller demonstrably installed custom minting
implementations, then later pointed sETH2 at incompatible Pool code. The refreshed destination
contracts do not establish an operating pARB bridge or an Arbitrum price feed.
Contracts and checkpoint
The refreshed PulseChain checkpoint is block 27,690,169, hash 
0x9805ab8cd6142ff6e69b82049318440b925e0c368880008809ac7c3f16943e70. The inherited comparison uses block
17,232,999. Historical event collection begins at 17,233,000.

Both Curve pools are minimal proxies pointing to 0x24d937143d3f5cf04c72ba112735151a8cae2262. Its PulseChain
runtime exactly matches the deployed bytecode in the saved, verified Ethereum explorer page. The
same comparison confirms that the PulseChain runtime at E68 is the verified StakeWise Pool, not
StakedEthT oken. These are exact byte comparisons, rather than names inferred from an explorer label.
The earlier Safe census found a change from 4-of-7 to 1-of-8, with 0xa8ed85b1d441da00270ecc6dc3600f3cba9d4a03
both an owner and an enabled module; the original owners remained. The refreshed ProxyAdmin
ownership and admin-slot reads independently establish the downstream upgrade path. They do not
establish exclusive human control or ownership of Curve LP shares.
What the three supplied transactions establish
MINTER_ROLE means permission to create new token units. It is a named access-control role
stored by a contract, not collateral, a token or a bridge. A mint function may require membership of that
role and any additional conditions its implementation imposes. Granting the role does not itself move an
asset across chains or prove backing. The role identifier is a hash of its name; its role members are the
addresses allowed to use it.

The Safe changed all three token
implementations: rETH2 and SWISE
returned to their inherited
implementations; sETH2 was explicitly
pointed to E68 Pool code.
The first two receipts contain RoleGranted events whose role identifier equals Keccak-256 of MINTER_ROLE.
Getter reads immediately after the June transaction confirm a8ed as the single member of that role on
both sETH2 and rETH2, and confirm functioning sETH2 ERC20 getters at that historical checkpoint. The
custom implementation bytecodes contain ERC20 and mint(address,uint256) dispatch entries and minter-
specific checks. The custom source is unverified, so selector presence alone is not a complete
reconstruction of the minting path, collateral rules or caps.
The role was followed by actual issuance. Three receipt-verified a8ed transactions called the sETH2
proxy's mint(address,uint256,address) selector 0x0d4d1513, creating 1,000,000, 1,000,000,000,000 and 
2,000,000,000,000 sETH2 for a8ed. The transactions are 
0x160bc7b4716036f34c73b42b609347a6a0ccafba0c28ecf4c2e27df7adb87176, 
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 407

0xc15b9e1bdd1c4607d39a1abf74ee8df669e6fb5f2809937fcb2253ad7b66bb37 and 
0xa895ca0985edafbf173f759dbee2b1183bb973400db0055a9efc234891aa5e9c. Their successful historical traces show
direct local calls from a8ed, delegated custom token logic, and rETH2 checkpoint calls. They show no
incoming L2 messenger, bridge call or collateral-token transfer in those mint transactions. An off-chain
financing arrangement or separately held backing is not excluded. The amounts are nominal sETH2
units, not verified ETH or dollar backing.
The third transaction directly explains the current sETH2 failure. Its inherited implementation was 
0x41bcac23e4db058d8d7aabe2fccdae5f01fe647a. It is not a case of confusing the token proxy with the separate
deposit-pool proxy. Pool code has staking and validator functions, but lacks the ERC20 entry points
expected at the token address. The evidence establishes the explicit incompatible implementation
selection; it does not establish the operator's reason for choosing it.
The deposit pool was separately swept
On 19 June 2026 at 06:09:25 UTC, transaction 
0x05f045f7ab0bf56a2d3c728a63c45342db5a7bb88783eb14cc5088c8f36e45ea upgraded the deposit pool to 2ced through
the Reality module, Safe and ProxyAdmin. The new runtime is 315 bytes. Inspection shows a single
dispatched sweep(address) function using the proxy's entire native balance as payment value, with no
caller authorization check in that implementation. It contains no ERC20 collateral intake, token issuance
or oracle integration.
At 06:11:15 UTC, transaction index 0 of block 26,822,460, 
0xbed4d20a304c487b23c6035afeac88acd84c7ff029135c0366b3b8be72ac8ad4, caused the deposit pool to transfer 
167,165,746.693072211927428963 PLS to 0x547a396e22f06735aad0e54820ae10137e5ae792. The transaction
succeeded; the internal transfer value and before/after native balances corroborate the amount.
The previously identified Reality-module sweep167 call, transaction 
0x8cd90d9cac79ce6b4e1a38fe53fdacd264fb7b737b084e3abd29c534a25e7390, was index 14 in that same block. It
called the pool with recipient 0x7563550940b136ddcd553a279cf025f704e7cf5b, but transferred zero, because the
pool was already empty. Its replayed state difference does not show a pool-balance change. The
evidence distinguishes the actual recipient from the later proposed recipient; common ownership and
transaction intent are unverified. These are native PLS amounts, not ETH amounts or dollar valuations.
This sweep is a deposit-pool cash withdrawal. Curve liquidity changes require separate pool-specific
evidence.
Observed Curve activity
The selected postfork Curve event queries completed without errors for both exact pool addresses and
the matched implementation's five liquidity/exchange signatures. Pair A returned no selected activity. Its
inherited LP supply and both token balances were already zero, so its present emptiness does not
establish a postfork withdrawal. Pair B returned three deposits and three swaps, with no matching LP
withdrawal events. Its inherited direct stETH balance was 0.099824936700059819, compared with about
9.10 now. The broader token-mint census has eight query errors in other ranges; it is not a complete
token issuance census. A separate error-free sETH2 query over the custom implementation period
returned the three direct mints above, all verified against receipts and historical traces.
On 2 August 2026, address 0x0c0330d30038ca28b99c1d1f1e92bf3e287c8f17 deposited 
210,411,070.397572542914872665 sETH2 and zero stETH into pair B in transaction 
0x792818f827a143bc11584f2698f47553152f28eca4bce3f41d021f000cf3552e. Its trace confirms Curve used the existing
sETH2 address and delegated to the custom 0257 implementation. This proves that large quantities of
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 408

the token could enter Curve under the changed implementation. It does not establish that those
deposited units came from the three a8ed mints, or that the depositor and minter share a human
controller.
The subsequent three swaps went from stETH into sETH2: 1 stETH purchased about 149.87 million
sETH2; 3 purchased about 28.99 million; 5 purchased about 10.18 million. This observed direction
supplied stETH to the pool. It is not evidence of those trades extracting stETH to finance pDAI purchases.
The enormous unit disparity is consistent with pool imbalance and is incompatible with treating this
history as execution at one ETH per sETH2.
What Curve accepts and how it prices trades
The matched Curve implementation sets two coin addresses and rate multipliers at initialization. It reads
each configured token's balanceOf(pool) for balances and computes quotes from those reserves,
amplification and fees. Transfers use the configured token addresses. The inspected implementation has 
no external price-feed input or Arbitrum oracle hook. Initialization is guarded against repetition;
its ABI exposes no coin replacement setter.
Consequently, sending an unrelated bridged ERC20 to a pool does not count it as sETH2. Matching a
name, symbol or claimed price is insufficient. Changing the StakeWise deposit pool does not change
Curve's coin list. Changing the logic at the existing sETH2 token address could preserve Curve's
accepted address, provided the replacement correctly implements balances, transfers, storage and
issuance.
The installed Pool implementation does not expand a Curve coin slot into a list of collateral assets. It
currently prevents the token reads on which both Curve pairs depend. Restoring working token logic
would be an additional authorized change, not a function of the current Pool code.
Where an L2 asset could fit
An operator could design an issuer that accepts several bridged assets and creates one fungible sETH2
claim at the existing token address:
L2 asset A ── authenticated bridge ──┐
L2 asset B ── authenticated bridge ──┼─ accepting issuer ── existing sETH2
L2 asset C ── authenticated bridge ──┘                         │
                                                             ▼
                                                funded sETH2/stETH Curve pair
This is a proposed adapter route. Curve would still have one sETH2 coin and one stETH coin. The multiple
underlying assets would be accounted for by the issuer, with its valuation, mint limits, redemption policy
and obligations. A token that cannot be authenticated or valued could still be admitted by a permissive
custom issuer, but that admission alone would not create backing or independent purchasing power.
An authenticated cross-chain message could alternatively authorize minting at the local token address.
The historical minter changes establish local issuance permissions; they do not identify a pARB
messenger, gateway mint function, source deployment or successful message carrying an L2 asset into
sETH2. A controller with local mint authority may not need an L2 transaction to issue tokens, depending
on the implementation's additional checks.
At the refreshed checkpoint, the copied Arbitrum router selects its standard ERC20 gateway for
sETH2. That gateway computes source counterpart 0xc0f8bc165b23b3c91248bde174480d536fc7a8c5; the custom
gateway's sETH2 mapping is zero. A calculated counterpart is not evidence of source deployment.
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 409

Ordinary standard-gateway settlement releases the existing destination token from escrow; this does not
establish a new direct bridge-mint route. The destination sETH2 balance getter currently reverts, so its
escrow quantity cannot be certified by that getter.
An oracle could inform a future issuer's conversion rate, but it would not directly set this Curve pool's
executable price. One dollar of stable collateral and one ETH-denominated sETH2 claim are different
units; valuation, buffers and redemption must handle that difference. Swaps obtain only the
counterasset inventory actually available. At this checkpoint pair A has no LP supply or stETH, pair B has
about 9.10 local stETH, and the sETH2-dependent quote path is broken. These observations do not
support a currently operating large financing route.
Evidence and reproduction
Raw requests, responses, historical traces and source snapshots are under artifacts/pulsechain-stakewise-
proxy-20261002/. The canonical upstream identities are StakeWise's published deployment list. Exact
runtime comparisons use the saved verified explorer pages for E68 Pool and Curve's shared
implementation.
Explicit manifests under Research/experiments/ are pulsechain_stakewise_proxy_routes_20261002.json, 
pulsechain_stakewise_proxy_history_20261002.json, pulsechain_stakewise_trace_reads_20261002.json, 
pulsechain_stakewise_custom_minter_getters_20261002.json, pulsechain_stakewise_curve_activity_20261002.json and 
pulsechain_stakewise_curve_inherited_20261002.json. Getter collection uses Research/scripts/
probe_pulsechain_routes.py --calls <manifest> --block <checkpoint> --output <new-file>. Event collection uses 
Research/scripts/collect_pulsechain_events.py --manifest <manifest> --output <new-file>. Historical minter
getters use block 0x1996d79; the fork-boundary getters use 0x106f467 and are saved in curve-fork-
boundary.json. The earlier curve-inherited.json actually sampled block 17,233,447 and is excluded from
fork-boundary comparisons. Frozen evidence is not overwritten. No mint, transfer, upgrade or setter was
simulated or broadcast.
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 410
